human_topics.HD01: Bipartite schedule/channel compatibility with a separate accessibility penalty; administrative work can continue without delivery.
human_topics.HD02: Route/allocation compatibility plus an independently chosen speed-burden frontier under essential service demand.
human_topics.HD03: Three-interface identifier interoperability with an asymmetric confidentiality exposure; neutral identifier reduces capacity.
human_topics.HD04: Batch separation creates a queue-dependent capacity gain; over-verification can consume delivery time.
human_topics.HP01: Recipient-set union with overlap and inaccessible unverified broadcasts; redundancy can crowd out useful coverage.
human_topics.HP02: Usable-payment completion with staged release, heterogeneous access and asymmetric verification error.
human_topics.HP03: Staffing/environment substitution with coercive high-throughput and supportive routes; over-briefing displaces care.
human_topics.HP04: Nonlinear shared-load trip with partial independent fallback and comfort burdens; more local output can destroy joint output.
human_topics.HP05: Duplicate issue consumes inventory in addition to recipient overlap; complementarity of disjoint lists competes with a mixed outreach route.
human_topics.HP06: Noncommutative process order encoded by simultaneous schedule commitments; closure prevents action burden but loses all service.
human_topics.HP07: Evidence granularity/review compatibility with reachable notice as completion and privacy costs attached to broad publication.
human_topics.HP08: Two parallel bottleneck chains with cross-channel allocation; balanced capacity incurs limited burdens but enables otherwise impossible useful service.
